summary.title: MQTT broker from scratch # 3 - Server
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build the server layer of a C MQTT 3.1.1 broker using epoll, with accept/read/write callbacks, packet framing, and a logging utility.
keywords: build a message broker in c
takeaways: The server exposes a minimal start_server(addr, port) entry point and uses epoll with configurable max events and timeout.
Three I/O callbacks (on_accept, on_read, on_write) re-arm the socket for reading or writing based on handler return codes.
recv_packet reads the MQTT fixed header byte by byte, decodes the remaining length, and reads the full packet before dispatch.
Command handlers are mapped in a table indexed by MQTT packet type, with NULL entries for unsupported types.
Outgoing PUBLISH packets are sent to each subscriber of a topic, with QoS adjusted to each subscriber's level.
summary.summary: This part of the series implements the server side of a MQTT 3.1.1 broker in C. It defines a small server header exposing start_server, then adds accept, read, and write callbacks driven by an epoll loop, with re-arming of sockets depending on handler return codes. It also covers packet reception with remaining-length decoding, a bytestring helper, generic utilities including logging, and a periodic stats-publishing task that sends PUBLISH packets to subscribers. The page is code-heavy and the text ends mid-sentence, so some details (such as publish_stats itself) are not shown.
